newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices dive with returned production.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices dive with returned production.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices eroded several cents Monday as news surfaced that more than one billion cubic feet per day of gas production had been restored following Hurricane Danny that lashed the Gulf Coast late last week.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices fell about nine cents to $2.15-2.18 per mmBtu at Henry Hub.
ANR Pipeline (150 mmcfd), Transco (100 mmcfd), Tennessee (600 mmcfd) and Stingray (71 mmcfd) all reported that gas flows on their systems were restored.

Columbia Gulf, which reported 270 mmcfd cut last week, said it expects production to be fully restored later today. The company said about 150 mmcfd of gas was still missing from the gas plant in Venice, La.
Duke Energy also reported that most of its gas flows were back to normal. Less than 100 mmcfd of gas was still being cut on Texas Eastern but was expected back shortly.
In south Texas, prices similarly slumped nine cents to about $2.10-2.12.
In the Permian Basin market, prices also fell nine cents to $2.05-2.06, while southern California border also eased a few cents to about $2.20.

The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada returned to service late Friday, while the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 unit, in southern California, was beginning to contribute to the grid early Monday.
Meanwhile, the adjacent unit 2, rated 1,070 MW, was running around 70 percent power while operators correct a problem with one of its feedwater pumps.
In the Midwest, prices dropped six cents to $2.05-2.06. Chicago city-gate gas was also weaker at $2.23-2.24.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate lost more than 10 cents to $2.37-2.42 at M3 and Zone 6.
